rationale: Continuing the authorized source work on the deferred transport surface: reading the connection lifecycle and the inbound dispatch path, which were the two largest unread blocks after the previous step. Reading only; no defect is asserted, no behavior edge is established, and no obligation is created.

feedback.answered: The outbound connection lifecycle and the inbound dispatch are now sourced. Outbound: getConn reuses a pooled connection for the target when one is available and otherwise dials through the StreamLayer with n.timeout, wrapping the connection in a buffered writer plus a msgpack encoder/decoder (net_transport.go 403-430); genericRPC sends the typed RPC and then calls decodeResponse, returning the connection to the pool only when the response decoded cleanly (496-506), so a connection whose response failed mid-stream is released rather than pooled; returnConn keeps at most maxPool connections per target and releases the rest (434-446); InstallSnapshot deliberately never reuses its connection (509-511). Inbound: each accepted connection runs the handle command loop, which reads one type byte, decodes the typed request into an RPC with a one-buffered response channel (640-716), classifies an AppendEntries as a heartbeat only when the term is non-zero, a leader address is present and the previous-log coordinate, entry list and commit index are all zero (665-680), routes a heartbeat to the callback snapshot taken under the mutex when one is installed (724-733), and otherwise blocks on the consumer channel send with a shutdown escape before waiting for the response and writing the error string followed by the response on the same connection (735-767). That per-connection serialisation is what makes the pipeline's FIFO response-order assumption hold.
remaining: The consumer channel's capacity and the resulting back-pressure policy were not read, so how many RPCs can queue before a connection blocks is unknown.
getPooledConn's body was not read, so whether a pooled connection can ever be handed to two callers concurrently is unknown.

StreamLayer and its implementations are still unread: TCPTransport's listener/dialer, TLS configuration wiring, the stream context used by CloseStreams/getStreamContext, and how a fatal listener error is surfaced.

InmemTransport's in-process delivery and ordering semantics are still unread; inmem_transport.go is the transport the captured tests exercise, so its assumptions matter to how the repo's own evidence is produced.

The heartbeat classification is read but not evaluated: it treats any AppendEntries with zero previous-log coordinate, no entries and commit index zero as a heartbeat, and whether that is exactly the shape the replication goroutine emits was not re-checked against the leader side here.

Previously recorded open items are unchanged: installSnapshot watermark reachability from a legal leader history, the compacted-leader variant of the truncation-failure case, and execution corroboration of the two reading-based consequences.
feedback.rationale: Recorded as feedback because it narrows an existing deferred surface with read source rather than establishing a requirement; the surface stays deferred because the pool internals, consumer back-pressure, StreamLayer/TCP wiring and the in-memory transport remain unread.
